newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cocaine, crack users get unequal punishment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cocaine, crack users get unequal punishment.

text.p: Stiffer U.S. prison sentences mandated for possession of crack cocaine than for for holding powdered versions of the drug are inappropriate and should be changed, researchers said on Tuesday.

Abusers who snort or inject cocaine often use it as a "gateway" drug to readily available "crack" and offenders as well as society as a whole would be better served by treatment rather than by meting out long sentences, two psychiatrists wrote in the Journal of the American Medical Association.

"Both forms of cocaine can lead to a lack of control over use and the same psychological, social, legal, and physiological consequences ... Although crack cocaine has been linked with crime to a greater extent than cocaine hydrochloride (the powdered form), many of these crimes are associated with the addiction to cocaine," Dorothy Hatsukami of the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis and Marian Fischman of Columbia University in New York wrote.

Sentencing guidelines passed by Congress in 1986 call for a first-time offender to get a minimum of five years in prison for possession of five grams of crack, or 50-200 doses, while a similar offender would have to be caught with 500 grams of cocaine hydrochloride, 10,000 doses, to get the same sentence.

Crack is made by mixing powdered cocaine with another alkaline substance such as sodium bicarbonate to convert it to a base and then heating it to form waxy chunks or "rocks." Because crack is more readily available in inner cities, its use is more prevalent among blacks and other minorities, leading to longer sentences for those groups, a disparity that has raised objections among civil rights advocates.

The researchers said cocaine use began in the 1970s as a province primarily of white, middle-class users. They cited 1993 federal statistics that showed 69 percent of cocaine users were white, 15 percent black and 13 percent Hispanic, and that most often the drug was snorted in powdered form.
